hard_courses.name: Software Engineering
hard_courses.description: Introduction to the software engineering process and software lifecycle. Covers project management, requirements, architecture, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance phase activities in team based projects.

hard_courses.name: Internetworking
hard_courses.description: Global Internet: design principles, layering, protocol design/analysis. Networked applications, Internet structure/architecture, Protocols for transport/congestion control, network layer/routing, link layer/MAC. Network security. EE 450

hard_courses.name: Calculus I
hard_courses.description: Limits; continuity, derivatives and applications; antiderivatives; the fundamental theorem of calculus; exponential and logarithmic functions. Satisfies New General Education in Category F: Quantitative Reasoning

hard_courses.name: Introduction to Embedded Systems
hard_courses.description: Information representations, embedded programming, digital and serial I/O, analog-to-digital conversion, and interrupt mechanisms. Elementary analog, logic and state-machine design.

hard_courses.name: Capstone: Design and Construction of Large Software Systems
hard_courses.description: Group project with an outside stakeholder to develop real-world software solutions to large-scale problems. Topics include software engineering, professional preparation, and recent computer science research.

elective_courses.name: Computer Graphics
elective_courses.description: Computer graphics, OpenGL, 2D and 3D transformations, Bézier splines, computer animation, rendering including ray tracing, shading and lighting, artistic rendering, virtual reality, visualization.

elective_courses.name: Native Console Multiplayer Game Development
elective_courses.description: Implementation of AAA style multiplayer game running on consoles and DX11. Console development in native C++, console SDKs, engine components, gameplay, networking, data prediction/replication.

elective_courses.name: Game Prototyping
elective_courses.description: Developing games or technology based on current and relevant special topics.

elective_courses.name: Computer and Network Security
elective_courses.description: A broad overview of security threats and defenses, security systems and functionalities. Includes homeworks and in-class exercises to provide practical experience working with such systems.

elective_courses.name: Foundations of Robotics
elective_courses.description: Designing and programming mobile robots; sensors, effectors, basic control theory, control architectures, planning, some advanced topics, illustrations of state-of-the-art. Weekly robot programming labs; final project. Crosslisted as EE 445

elective_courses.name: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development
elective_courses.description: Hands-on AI: data mining, machine learning, optimization and fairness in the context of applications with environmental and societal benefit.

elective_courses.name: Foundations of Machine Learning
elective_courses.description: Algorithms for learning behavior from data, including both mathematical underpinnings and practical techniques. Covers supervised learning, deep learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning. EE 460

elective_courses.name: Theory of Computation
elective_courses.description: History of the theory of computing, foundational theorems and theoretical frameworks of computer science, solvable and unsolvable problems.

elective_courses.name: Cryptography: Secure Communication and Computation
elective_courses.description: Introduction to modern Cryptography; mathematical/algorithmic studies of methods for protecting information in computer and communication systems: Public-Key Cryptosystems, zero-knowledge proofs, data privacy.

elective_courses.name: File and Database Management
elective_courses.description: File input/output techniques, basic methods for file organization, file managers, principles of databases, conceptual data models, and query languages.

elective_courses.name: Directed Research
elective_courses.description: Individual research and readings. Credit Restriction: Not available for graduate credit.

elective_courses.name: Special Topics
elective_courses.description: Selected topics in computer science.

elective_courses.name: Introduction to Digital Circuits
elective_courses.description: Digital system design and implementation; synchronous design of datapath and control; schematic/Verilog-based design, simulation, and implementation in Field Programmable Gate Arrays; timing analysis; semester-end project.

elective_courses.name: Parallel and Distributed Computation
elective_courses.description: Introduction to parallel programming techniques, models and optimization strategies; Application mapping to multi-core, accelerator, GPU and cloud platforms; High Performance Computing and Data Science applications. Crosslisted as CSCI 452

elective_courses.name: Introduction to System-on-Chip
elective_courses.description: Design flow, tools, and issues related to System/Network-on-Chip (S/Noc) design for real-time embedded systems with applications in mobile, cloud, aerospace, and medical electronics. Crosslisted as CSCI 454

elective_courses.name: Computer Systems Organization
elective_courses.description: Register Transfer level machine organization; performance; arithmetic; pipelined processors; exceptions, out-of-order and speculative execution, cache, virtual memory, multi-core multi-threaded processors, cache coherence. Crosslisted as CSCI 457

elective_courses.name: Embedded Systems Design Laboratory
elective_courses.description: Specification, design, implementation, testing and documentation of a digital system project using embedded processors, programmable logic, analog I/O interfaces and application specific hardware. Capstone design experience. Credit Restriction: Not available for graduate credit

elective_courses.name: MOS VLSI Circuit Design
elective_courses.description: Analysis and design of digital MOS VLSI circuits including area, delay and power minimization. Laboratory assignments including design, layout, extraction, simulation and automatic synthesis.

elective_courses.name: Directed Research
elective_courses.description: Individual research and readings. Credit Restriction: Not available for graduate credit.

elective_courses.name: Special Topics
elective_courses.description: Course content will be selected each semester from current developments in the field of electrical engineering.

elective_courses.name: Numerical Methods
elective_courses.description: Rounding errors in digital computation; solution of linear algebraic systems; Newton’s method for nonlinear systems; matrix eigenvalues; polynomial approximation; numerical integration; numerical solution of ordinary differential equations. Crosslisted as CSCI 458

elective_courses.name: Cross-Platform App Development
elective_courses.description: Programming applications with dynamic graphical user interfaces. Topics include events, controls, resources, data bindings, styles and user experience. Crosslisted as CSCI 368

elective_courses.name: Video Game Programming
elective_courses.description: Underlying concepts and principles required for programming video games (topics include vectors, transformations, 3-D math, geometric primitives, matrices). Crosslisted as CSCI 380

elective_courses.name: Professional C++
elective_courses.description: Applications of advanced concepts in C++ including lambda expressions, templates, secure coding, parallel programming, writing performant code, CMake and continuous integration. Crosslisted as CSCI 435

elective_courses.name: Compiler Development
elective_courses.description: Practical applications of techniques used to develop a programming language compiler. Crosslisted as CSCI 439

elective_courses.name: Programming Game Engines
elective_courses.description: Techniques for building the core components of a game engine; 2-D/3-D graphics, collision detection, artificial intelligence algorithms, shading, programming input devices. Crosslisted as CSCI 487
